Kyle / Ops —

Quick status update following the 09:00 PT triage & 09:30 PT exec alignment:

What happened
- Between 07:45–08:30 PT we observed a sudden increase in queued requests to the US-west serving pool that correlated with elevated tokenization-heavy routes. Increased KV cache misses led to CPU-bound execution paths and elevated 5xx rates.

What we did
- Diverted 25% of traffic to an isolated canary pool at 08:22 PT — canary p95 ~320ms and error rate returned to baseline.
- Identified a recent kernel selection flag flip (internal optimization) that widened code-path heterogeneity for long-context requests. Toggled the flag off on the main pool at 08:50 PT; errors fell from 5.8% -> 0.6% by 09:10 PT.
- We kept the canary warm and progressively shifted traffic back; full normalization by 09:55 PT.

Customer comms & exec decisions
- We drafted a short customer-facing note (attached) and asked Apogee to publish a status page.
- Redwood execs agreed to a goodwill credit cap if remediation exceeded 90 minutes; we discussed immediate credits if customer escalation required. Sophie — we’ll follow up separately on details.

Open actions
- Post-mortem doc (owner: Aditya) due EOD 2028-03-06.
- Run a targeted workload test for long-context routes on the main pool to ensure no regression (owner: Karthik) — ETA 48 hours.
- Finalize customer comms and compensation language (owner: Marissa) — to send by 11:00 PT.

If you want a short executive note for your leadership, tell me the distribution list and we’ll tailor it. Appreciate the quick escalation — team was focused on restoring customer experience.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
